outcome: No result found in the window (26 January 2024 – present) that settles, partially settles, or moves the ZFC question of whether GCH holding below a strongly compact cardinal implies GCH holds everywhere. The only adjacent development, a negative answer under the negation of full AC (ZF, not ZFC), is both (a) a changed hypothesis rather than a case of the stated problem, and (b) mathematically published before the frozen revision date.
summary: The problem asks (in ZFC, as is standard for this list): if κ is strongly compact and GCH holds for all cardinals below κ, must GCH hold everywhere? Extensive searching (general web search, arXiv listings, Wikipedia's own 'Strongly compact cardinal' article, and targeted author searches for Apter, Gitik, Goldberg, Usuba, and others who work in this exact area) turned up no result in the ZFC setting that resolves, partially resolves, or moves a bound on this question since 26 January 2024. The one genuinely close-sounding item is Arthur Apter's work titled 'A Choiceless Answer to a Question of Woodin', presented as talks at the CUNY Set Theory Seminar (22 March 2024) and the Rutgers Logic Seminar (25 March 2024) — both inside the window. However, per multiple independent search syntheses, the underlying mathematical result is a negative answer to Woodin's question obtained in the *absence of the full Axiom of Choice* (i.e., in ZF rather than ZFC), and the underlying paper — 'A Note on a Question of Woodin', Bulletin of the Polish Academy of Sciences (Mathematics), vol. 71(2), 2023, pp. 115–121 — was published in 2023, before the frozen revision date of 26 January 2024. Two things follow. First, dropping full AC changes the hypotheses of the question rather than restricting its scope (it is not obtained by narrowing the domain of κ or the class of models within ZFC), so per §3.1 this is a related/variant problem, not a case of the stated one, and does not count as a change to this bullet even on its own terms. Second, even setting that aside, the actual first written argument predates the window; only the seminar talks recapitulating already-published 2023 work fall inside it, which is not itself a new result. Other adjacent literature found (Goldberg's 2021 'Strongly compact cardinals and ordinal definability', settling a different question of Woodin's — nonexistence of an elementary embedding from HOD to itself under the HOD hypothesis and a strongly compact cardinal; the Ultrapower-Axiom-implies-GCH-above-a-supercompact result, which is conditional on UA, a different and stronger hypothesis than 'GCH holds below a strongly compact cardinal', and predates 2024 in any case) is all either off-topic for this specific bullet or outside the window. No AI system appears anywhere in any of the sources checked; this is a purely human, and in fact largely inactive, corner of set theory in the relevant window. I judge the record complete and well-evidenced for a 'nothing happened' conclusion, with confidence high.
competing_reading: If one reads the Wikipedia statement as not implicitly restricted to ZFC (the statement as given doesn't say 'ZFC' explicitly, only 'strongly compact cardinal' and 'GCH'), one might argue the choiceless negative answer is a legitimate case of the stated problem rather than a variant, since it is literally a model where the antecedent (strongly compact κ, GCH below κ) holds and the consequent (GCH everywhere) fails. Under that reading the status would be `open_stale` (negative answer, but the underlying paper is from 2023, before the frozen revision) rather than `open`. I judge the ZFC reading more faithful to how this list and the surrounding literature treat the problem — Woodin's question is uniformly stated and discussed in the ZFC context in every secondary source found, with the choiceless work explicitly framed by its own author as a distinct, weaker-hypothesis question — but flag this as the strongest case for a different classification.
what_would_settle_it: A definitive resolution would require either (a) locating the original source in which Woodin posed this question (a talk, paper, or problem list from the 1980s/1990s) to see whether it explicitly assumes full AC/ZFC, which would settle the competing_reading question, or (b) finding a genuinely new ZFC-context paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that addresses the strongly-compact-cardinal GCH question directly — none was found despite multiple search strategies.
